name: Cyber-Physical & Autonomous Vehicle Security
description: Security of cyber-physical systems, ICS/SCADA, robotics, drones, and autonomous/connected vehicles.
narrative:
The earliest work in this list (2018) splits along two fronts that defined the field's opening moves. One front targets the physical-sensing layer of cyber-physical systems: papers like "Injected and Delivered: Fabricating Implicit Control over Actuation Systems by Spoofing Inertial Sensors" (USENIX 2018) and "All Your GPS Are Belong To Us" (USENIX 2018) showed that attackers could manipulate the analog signals systems trust — inertial sensors, GPS — to seize control of drones and mislead road navigation. The other front is defensive and process-aware: "Detecting Attacks Against Robotic Vehicles: A Control Invariant Approach" (CCS 2018) and "Learning from Mutants" (S&P 2018) introduced the idea that physical control laws and learned invariants can flag when a CPS is being manipulated, while "Scission" (CCS 2018) fingerprinted senders on automotive buses. A third theme arrived via "BlackIoT" (USENIX 2018), which reframed commodity IoT as a weapon against the power grid.

The 2019-2020 period is dominated by a breakthrough that reorients the whole area toward autonomous-vehicle perception. "Adversarial Sensor Attack on LiDAR-based Perception in Autonomous Driving" (CCS 2019) — by far the most cited paper here — demonstrated that spoofed LiDAR points could fool 3D object detection, and "Towards Robust LiDAR-based Perception" (USENIX 2020) followed with a general black-box attack plus countermeasures. Sensor-spoofing matured into a science: "Trick or Heat?" (CCS 2019) and "Hall Spoofing" (USENIX 2020) hit temperature and Hall sensors, and "SoK: A Minimalist Approach to Formalizing Analog Sensor Security" (S&P 2020) finally formalized this growing attack class. Defenses kept pace, moving from ad-hoc detection toward principled physical invariants in "SAVIOR" (USENIX 2020) and "RVFuzzer" (USENIX 2019), which fuzzed robotic-vehicle control software to find input-validation bugs.

By 2021-2023 the perception attacks became more realistic and more complete. "Invisible for both Camera and LiDAR" (S&P 2021) broke multi-sensor fusion — the very design assumed to be robust because it combines modalities — while "Poltergeist" (S&P 2021) and "I Can See the Light" (CCS 2021) attacked cameras through acoustics and invisible light, and "Phantom of the ADAS" (CCS 2020) tricked production driver-assistance systems with split-second projected images. The community also matured methodologically: "DriveFuzz" (CCS 2022) brought systematic fuzzing to whole autonomous-driving stacks, "SoK: Security and Privacy in the Age of Commercial Drones" (S&P 2021) consolidated the drone literature, and "PLA-LiDAR" (S&P 2023) pushed physical laser attacks to richer 3D-detection targets. Across the same span, the smart-home/IoT thread stayed active with "HAWatcher" (USENIX 2021) and "IoTSafe" (NDSS 2021) enforcing safety via discovered physical interactions. The arc, then, runs from isolated single-sensor spoofs to attacks on fused, learning-based perception — met by an increasingly formal toolkit of invariants, attestation, and fuzzing.

milestones.title: Injected and Delivered: Fabricating Implicit Control over Actuation Systems by Spoofing Inertial Sensors
milestones.note: showed analog spoofing of inertial sensors could implicitly seize control of actuation systems, seeding the sensor-attack research line

milestones.title: Detecting Attacks Against Robotic Vehicles: A Control Invariant Approach
milestones.note: established control-invariant monitoring as the foundational defense paradigm for robotic-vehicle attack detection

milestones.title: Adversarial Sensor Attack on LiDAR-based Perception in Autonomous Driving
milestones.note: the field's most-cited work, which proved spoofed LiDAR points can fool autonomous-driving 3D perception and reoriented research toward AV sensing

milestones.title: SAVIOR: Securing Autonomous Vehicles with Robust Physical Invariants
milestones.note: advanced defense from ad-hoc detection to robust physical invariants spanning aerial, sea, and ground vehicles

milestones.title: SoK: A Minimalist Approach to Formalizing Analog Sensor Security
milestones.note: formalized the sprawling analog-sensor-attack literature into a coherent framework

milestones.title: Invisible for both Camera and LiDAR: Security of Multi-Sensor Fusion based Perception in Autonomous Driving Under Physical-World Attacks
milestones.note: broke the assumption that multi-sensor fusion is inherently robust, raising the bar for perception security

milestones.title: DriveFuzz: Discovering Autonomous Driving Bugs through Driving Quality-Guided Fuzzing
milestones.note: brought systematic quality-guided fuzzing to entire autonomous-driving stacks, maturing the field's testing methodology

milestones.title: PLA-LiDAR: Physical Laser Attacks against LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicle
milestones.note: extended physical laser attacks to richer 3D object-detection targets, marking the current state of perception-attack realism
